claims.text: Doxycycline: healthy outpatients, alone as one monotherapy option;
claims.quote: For healthy outpatient adults without comorbidities listed below or risk factors for antibiotic resistant pathogens, we recommend (Table 3): • amoxicillin 1 g three times daily (strong recommendation, moderate quality of evidence), or • doxycycline 100 mg twice daily

claims.text: with comorbidities, with a beta-lactam in place of a macrolide.
claims.quote: Beta-lactam (cefpodoxime, cefuroxime, amoxicillin, or amoxicillin/clavulanic acid) plus either Macrolide or doxycycline
claims.locator: Table: Antibiotic Therapy for Bacterial CAP in Adults, II. Outpatients, comorbidities present

claims.text: Influenza: oseltamivir (oral) or zanamivir (inhaled) for 5 days, best within 48 hours of onset;
claims.quote: For influenza, neuraminidase inhibitors (oral oseltamivir, aerosolized zanamivir) given for 5 days reduce the duration and severity of symptoms in patients who develop influenza infection, regardless of the duration of illness before symptom onset. However, initiating treatment within 48 hours of onset has been associated with the best outcomes

claims.text: peramivir IV or baloxavir oral as single doses;
claims.quote: Alternatively, IV peramivir or oral baloxavir started within 48 hours of symptom onset can be given as single doses.

claims.text: hospitalized patients get a neuraminidase inhibitor even after 48 hours.
claims.quote: Patients hospitalized with confirmed influenza infection should receive neuraminidase inhibitors; in such patients, administration may be beneficial even if initiated 48 hours after symptom onset
